title: pg_basebackup forwards a tar member trailer using a pointer that buffering already advanced past it
live_proof: inspection at the 17.5 pin. bbstreamer_tar.c:220-222 calls `bbstreamer_buffer_until(streamer, &data, &len, mystreamer->pad_bytes_expected)`, which takes `data` and `len` BY ADDRESS. Its body at bbstreamer.h:174-196 reaches `bbstreamer_buffer_bytes(streamer, data, len, target_bytes - buflen)` at :194, and that helper copies the bytes into the streamer's own buffer while advancing `*data` forward and reducing `*len` by the same amount. So on return `data` points PAST the padding, and when the padding completed the chunk, `len` is 0 and `data` is one past the end of the caller's input. bbstreamer_tar.c:225-228 then passes that advanced `data` with length `pad_bytes_expected` to the next streamer, which reads pad_bytes_expected bytes from beyond the input. Upstream replaces the argument with `mystreamer->base.bbs_buffer.data`, the buffer the padding was actually copied into; the pin passes `data`.
object: the input chunk pg_basebackup received from the server, below which nothing is mapped
lifetime_ender: n/a -- the object is live; the defect is a read past its end
shape: a by-address helper advances the caller's cursor and the caller then reuses the old meaning of it
fidelity: real buffering helpers, transcribed caller, REPRODUCED. bbstreamer_buffer_until and bbstreamer_buffer_bytes are copied verbatim from bbstreamer.h:156-196, including the `*data += nbytes` that is the whole defect; the forwarding call is bbstreamer_tar.c:225-228 transcribed, passing `data` as the pin does rather than bbs_buffer.data as the fix does. StringInfo is a stand-in for src/common/stringinfo.c because the buffer's growth policy takes no part in the defect -- all that matters is that the bytes are copied somewhere else. Not reproduced: the tar parsing that reaches BBSTREAMER_MEMBER_TRAILER and computes pad_bytes_expected, which needs a server streaming a base backup.

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: SIGPROT(34) -- CHERI-DETECTED. The next streamer reads pad_bytes_expected bytes from a pointer bbstreamer_buffer_until had already advanced to one past the end of the chunk, so the first byte read is already out of bounds. CheriBSD riscv64-purecap, static build, 2026-10-06. The PG_DEFECT marker printed before the fault, so the setup provably ran and the fault is the defective access rather than something earlier.

host-asan.oracle: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow, READ of size 1, "0 bytes to the right of 24-byte region", in pgclient_consume_content (the next streamer) called from case.c:58. The 24-byte region is the input chunk and 24 is pad_bytes_expected. Two notes print first and establish the mechanism rather than asserting it: remaining_len=0 and data_past_end=1, i.e. bbstreamer_buffer_until consumed the whole chunk and left `data` exactly one past its end, which is the pointer bbstreamer_tar.c:225 then forwards. Host build, 2026-10-06.

status: reproduced on the host under ASan and CHERI-DETECTED on the purecap arm, both 2026-10-06; the two Capstone arms cannot host it (see the corpus note)
